title: Local Mechanisms of Compositional Generalization in Conditional Diffusion
role: Theory of when scores compose: disjoint factorization equals local scores, with an orthogonality check and SDXL measurements
reads: EDM2 U-Net on noisy 128 px CLEVR with location or colour conditions; SDXL post-FFN transformer block features for 24 prompts
trained_on: CLEVR with 1 to K objects, 500,000 images per object count; SDXL and Matryoshka used pretrained
score_enters: No external gradient; CLEVR sampling uses raw conditional scores with no guidance, and the local model denoises patches
adding_scores: Exact if and only if the distribution factorizes over disjoint pixel or feature sets, each read by one condition (Lemma 1); orthogonal score differences are a necessary check (Lemma 2)
properties: Counting and position measured on CLEVR; binding, spatial relation, size and prompt match not measured
unseen: partly: object count is held out on CLEVR (trained on 1 to 3, tested up to 12), with no new object types or colours
headline: Trained on 1 to 3 CLEVR objects, Kmax (objects drawn reliably) is 7 with all objects labelled against 2 with one label, and enforcing local scores lifts the one-label model to 9; SDXL feature cosine is 0.41 to 0.47 within category and 0.27 to 0.33 between
copy_or_avoid: Copy the Lemma 2 cosine check on cat and dog U-Net differences before training; avoid expecting a whole-image sentence score to move position (inferred)
model: EDM2 U-Net on CLEVR; SDXL base 1.0; Matryoshka Diffusion Model

disagreements.claim: SDXL shows quantitative evidence of feature-space local conditional scores
disagreements.source: this paper, p. 9, read against its own Lemma 2, p. 7
disagreements.paper_says: Lemma 2 requires exactly zero cosine between different conditions, while the measured between-category cosine is 0.27 to 0.33; the evidence offered is a within over between ratio (inferred)

disagreements.claim: Approximately compositional distributions become more compositional at higher noise
disagreements.source: this paper, p. 17, combining Lemma 3 and Lemma 4
disagreements.paper_says: Lemma 4 bounds KL from the marginal to a conditional at a fixed y, while Definition 3 uses the reverse argument order and conditions on the other pixels, which are also noised, so Lemma 4 does not directly bound Definition 3's errors (inferred)
